title: Best AlorAir Dehumidifier (2026): Sentinel vs. Storm Models
dek: Two families under one name — one for quietly guarding a crawl space, one for drying out a flood. Here's how to pick the right AlorAir.
description: The best AlorAir dehumidifier for 2026: Sentinel HDi65S and HD55 for crawl spaces, plus Storm LGR models for flood dry-outs, with reviews and buying tips.
intro: If you've looked into crawl-space encapsulation or water-damage cleanup, you've probably run into an AlorAir dehumidifier. The brand has become a favorite of encapsulation contractors and restoration crews, largely because it delivers near-commercial performance for a fraction of what legacy pro brands charge.

The catch is that AlorAir sells two very different product families. The **Sentinel** line is built to sit in a crawl space or basement and hold steady humidity for months. The **Storm** line uses Low Grain Refrigerant (LGR) technology to dry out a soaked building fast. Buy the wrong family and you'll either overspend on restoration gear or under-buy for a real flood.
Below we break down the AlorAir models most homeowners should consider, what owners say about them, and how to read AlorAir's two pint ratings.
topPicksLead: For most crawl spaces and basements, the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** is the AlorAir to buy: compact, self-draining, Wi-Fi connected and built to run unattended down to about 36°F.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S Wi-Fi Dehumidifier
pros: Compact body fits low-clearance crawl spaces
App alerts for faults and humidity swings
cons: Needs a Wi-Fi signal at the crawl hatch for alerts
Saturation rating on the box can mislead
products.whyWeLoveIt: The HDi65S is the right default across most of AlorAir's use cases. It's small enough for a crawl space, strong enough for a damp basement and self-draining enough to leave alone for months — and in a space you rarely visit, an alert on your phone means a stuck defrost cycle or clogged drain line gets caught in hours, not weeks.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 55 pints a day under AHAM conditions and 120 at saturation, for spaces up to about 1,300 square feet. The pump lifts water 19.6 feet, enough to reach daylight from most basements and crawls without a floor drain, and Wi-Fi adds app control and notifications. It's the current version of the HDi65, with the same pump and defrost hardware. Owner reviews most often praise how long it runs without attention. See how it compares with a pricier contractor favorite in our [AlorAir vs. Aprilaire](/compare/alorair-vs-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) comparison.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HD55 Dehumidifier
pros: Nearly the HDi65S's capacity for less
cons: Can't add a built-in pump later
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your crawl or basement has a sump or a low point to drain toward, the HD55 gets you almost the same drying power for less. Just confirm the drain route before you buy.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 53 pints AHAM and 113 at saturation, with the same auto-defrost as the pump models. Water leaves through a gravity hose, so the unit must sit above wherever the hose ends. A Wi-Fi version, the HD55S, adds app monitoring to the same platform.

products.name: AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme Dehumidifier
pros: LGR design keeps drying already-dry air
cons: Heavier and louder than a Sentinel
products.whyWeLoveIt: After a burst pipe or flood, you need to pull moisture out of drywall, framing and subfloors quickly. LGR refrigeration keeps extracting water at humidity levels where a standard unit stalls, which is exactly what a dry-out needs.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 85 pints AHAM and 180 at saturation, covering up to 2,300 square feet. Its pump lifts water 14.7 feet through a 19.6-foot hose, and it carries a five-year warranty. It costs a fraction of comparable legacy restoration units. See how it stacks up in our [commercial dehumidifier](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/) and [water damage](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-water-damage/) guides.

products.name: AlorAir Storm LGR 850 Dehumidifier
pros: Same 85-pint AHAM capacity as the Extreme
Lighter body for moving between jobs
cons: Still too much machine for routine use
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a one-time cleanup or a contractor hauling gear between sites, the LGR 850 delivers essentially the Extreme's drying power in a lighter, simpler package.
products.performance: It's rated at 85 pints AHAM and 180 at saturation, with operation down to 36°F — useful for a cold, unfinished basement after a spring flood. It skips some of the Extreme's extras to keep weight and cost down.

items.label: AHAM vs. saturation pints for the same HDi65S
Standard limited warranty on current Sentinel models

blocks.text: The first number trips up many shoppers. Saturation ratings are measured at 90°F and 90% humidity — flood conditions — while AHAM ratings use 80°F and 60%. Size and compare on AHAM pints.

We don't lab-test. We compare AlorAir's AHAM ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals and warranty terms, then read owner and contractor reviews for recurring issues such as pump failures, defrost problems and sensor drift. We also check the CPSC recall database.
We ranked models on how well they match the two jobs AlorAir targets — steady humidity control and fast restoration drying — then on drainage, cold-weather performance and monitoring.

sections.heading: What to look for in an AlorAir dehumidifier

items.label: Sentinel or Storm
items.text: Sentinel for ongoing control in a crawl space or basement; Storm for drying an actively wet building.

items.label: Pump or gravity
items.text: If you can't route a hose downhill to a drain, choose a pump model. Only the HD55 relies on gravity.

items.label: Wi-Fi for remote spaces
items.text: App alerts matter most in places you visit less than monthly.

items.label: AHAM pints
items.text: Compare the smaller number across brands. Our [crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) guide explains sizing.

items.label: Where you'll buy
items.text: AlorAir sells mainly online, so register the unit for warranty service as soon as it arrives.

sections.heading: Other AlorAir models: HD55S, HDi90, SLGR and Storm LGR 1250

items: **Sentinel HD55S** — the HD55 with Wi-Fi. A good fit if you can gravity-drain but still want alerts.
**Sentinel HDi90** — a larger Sentinel with a built-in pump for big basements and large sealed crawls where a 55-pint unit would run constantly.
**Sentinel SLGR** — brings LGR refrigeration to the Sentinel family for commercial spaces that need deeper drying than a standard Sentinel.
**Storm LGR 1250** — a bigger Storm model aimed at larger restoration and construction-drying jobs.

blocks.text: For most homes, these are step-ups rather than starting points. Begin with the HDi65S and size up only if the space is unusually large or wet. If you're installing in a crawl space, our [crawl space dehumidifier installation](/guides/crawl-space-dehumidifier-installation/) guide covers placement, drainage and vapor barriers.

Across owner and contractor reviews, the consistent praise is for long, unattended run times and strong performance in cold crawl spaces. The recurring complaints are about the pump: kinked or poorly routed hoses can trigger shutoffs, and a few owners report pump failures after several seasons. Because AlorAir sells mostly online, some reviewers note that warranty service means shipping or a phone diagnosis rather than a local store visit.

blocks.title: Is AlorAir a good brand?
blocks.text: For crawl spaces, basements and restoration, yes. It offers commercial-style features and a long warranty at prices well below legacy pro brands. The trade-off is limited big-box availability and online-only support.

The **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** is the best AlorAir dehumidifier for most crawl spaces and basements, with remote alerts built in. Choose the **HD55** if you can gravity-drain, and the **Storm LGR Extreme** or lighter **Storm LGR 850** if you're drying out a flood. For how AlorAir ranks against other names, see our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup.

faqs.q: What is the best AlorAir dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most homes, the Sentinel HDi65S: a compact 55-pint (AHAM) unit with a built-in pump, Wi-Fi alerts and auto-defrost to about 36°F. For flood restoration, the Storm LGR Extreme is AlorAir's top pick.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the AlorAir Sentinel HD55 and HD55S?
faqs.a: The HD55S adds Wi-Fi app control and alerts to the HD55 platform. Both drain by gravity rather than a built-in pump, so you need a downhill route for the hose.

faqs.q: What's the difference between AlorAir's Sentinel and Storm lines?
faqs.a: Sentinel models are compact units for ongoing humidity control in crawl spaces and basements. Storm models use LGR refrigeration to dry water-damaged buildings quickly.

faqs.q: Does the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Yes, the Extreme includes app connectivity along with its built-in pump. The lighter Storm LGR 850 drops some of those extras to cut weight and cost.
For crawl spaces, basements and restoration, they're widely used by contractors and well reviewed by owners. Common complaints center on pump hoses and online-only warranty service.

faqs.q: Why do AlorAir dehumidifiers list two pint ratings?
faqs.a: The larger saturation number is measured at 90°F and 90% humidity; the smaller AHAM figure at 80°F and 60%. Size on AHAM, since the saturation figure roughly doubles real-world capacity.

faqs.q: Where can I buy an AlorAir dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Mostly online, through Amazon and AlorAir's own store, plus some farm-supply and specialty retailers. Big-box stores rarely stock it, so register your unit with AlorAir for warranty service after purchase.
